subject: Compatibility sanity exception & staggered rollout plan for Beryl-6B variant
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Compatibility sanity exception & staggered rollout plan for Beryl-6B variant

Priya —

Quick summary: our runtime tests surfaced a tokenizer mismatch and a subtle KV-cache ordering difference when running the Beryl-6B quantized build (v6.1). The model itself looks fine in isolated runs, but our integration suite shows a 0.6% increase in decoding mismatches for long-context prompts (>2k tokens). That’s low but spikes in a couple of customer-specific prompt sets.

Ask: Can we approve a compatibility-sanctuary exception to allow a limited canary (staggered rollout) against production traffic while we apply a short compatibility shim? We need guidance on pin policy for the duration and a sign-off on the canary scope.

Attached: beryl-6b-compat-report.pdf, canary-runbook.md

Risks we’ve identified:
- Tokenization differences causing semantically equivalent but not byte-for-byte identical outputs (low business risk).
- Quantization kernel edge-case that increases latency by ~8% on T4-class hardware (cost/latency tradeoff).

Proposed mitigations:
1) 5% traffic canary per region for 7 days with immediate rollback trigger on error-rate > 0.5% or delta in completion quality metrics.
2) Telemetry hooks for token-level diffs and downstream gating (LLM score drop).
3) Pre-rolled fallback variant (Beryl-6B-v5.9) pinned for the canary cohort.

Next steps: need product/legal/ops alignment on pin window and customer communications.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Lead Platform Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-20T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Compatibility sanity exception & staggered rollout plan for Beryl-6B variant

Thanks Marcus — good writeup.

A few clarifying asks before I take this to Product and Legal for the exception window:
- Can you quantify which customer prompt-sets produced the spike (IDs or short descriptions)? We need to surface whether any active paid accounts are directly impacted.
- What’s the incremental cost exposure if latency rises by 8% during the canary? Put a rough $/100k tokens estimate so Sales can pre-empt questions.
- Confirm the rollback play: immediate pin back to v5.9 + roll-forward only after green telemetry for 72h.

Operational proposal (high level):
- Canary: 5% traffic for 7 days in us-west/us-east only.
- Pin: pin customer cohorts who opt-out to v5.9 for the canary duration.
- Escalation: auto-fallback to v5.9 if QoS triggers fire or if customer-reported regressions exceed 2 open tickets referencing generation quality within 48h.

I’ve sketched a proposed rollout schedule (attached: proposed-rollout-schedule.xlsx). I’ll loop in Product (Lauren) for impact on customers and Sales/CS if we need to proactively notify accounts (DataSage is already flagged).

If you can answer the three bullets above, I’ll push for exception approval with the suggested guards. Also planning a 30-min sync at 11:00 if you’re available to run the numbers.

—Priya
Priya Natarajan
Program Manager, Model Onboarding & Safety
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-20T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Compatibility sanity exception & staggered rollout plan for Beryl-6B variant

Priya / Marcus —

Quick tech notes to answer your questions:
- Affected prompt-sets: "legal-qa-longform", "datasage-reports-v2", and a subset of the "summarize-large-docs" workload. Those map to customer IDs: DS-110 (DataSage), INT-88, SUM-310.
- Cost exposure: on T4 the 8% latency uplift converts to ~ $0.014 / 1k tokens extra (ballpark). On A10 it’s negligible. If we run the canary on A10-heavy pools the cost delta drops to $0.004 / 1k tokens.
- Rollback: we can implement immediate pin via the routing policy; I recommend automatic pinning for users in the canary cohort until the rollback completes.

Mitigation plan:
1) Apply a small tokenizer normalization shim in front of the model that aligns whitespace/token boundaries for the three workloads. This is a low-risk patch and can be toggled in the serving layer.
2) Ship a quant-kernel tweak that avoids the edge-case branch; patch will add ~3% memory overhead but removes mismatch for long contexts.
3) If we still see residual mismatches, we keep the pin and schedule a full offline alignment job to re-tokenize training data (longer path).

I’ve attached a minimal compat patch (compat-patch.diff) and a short runbook for toggling the shim. If Product approves the one-week canary we can land the shim and run the canary within 48 hours.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Infra Engineer, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Emily Harris <emily@datasage.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-20T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Compatibility sanity exception & staggered rollout plan for Beryl-6B variant

Priya —

Thanks for the heads up. DataSage sees a fair amount of long-context summaries under DS-110. We’d prefer advance notice before any canary that could affect quality; can you confirm SLA impact (if any) and whether we can opt-out of the canary for our production traffic? Also, what’s the expected timeline to rollback if we see regressions?

We’re evaluating a renewal in Q4 and want to avoid surprises. Happy to join a quick sync if needed.

—Emily
Emily Harris
Head of ML Ops, DataSage

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Harris <emily@datasage.ai>
Date: 2027-06-20T15:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Compatibility sanity exception & staggered rollout plan for Beryl-6B variant

Team —

Decision and actions: approved for a controlled canary with the following firm guards. I’m documenting here so Legal/Product can reference.

1) Canary scope: 5% traffic, us-west/us-east, 7-day window. DataSage (DS-110) is explicitly excluded from the canary (they will be pinned to Beryl-6B-v5.9) per their request.
2) Telemetry/thresholds: auto-rollback triggers if token-level mismatch rate > 0.5% OR completion-quality delta > 2.0% compared to v5.9 baseline. Customer-ticket threshold: 2 open tickets referencing regen quality within 48h will also trigger rollback.
3) Pin policy: customers in the canary cohort will be pinned to v5.9 for the canary duration if they opt-out; default routing will send canary traffic to v6.1 only for the 5% cohort.
4) Mitigations: Dev will land the tokenizer shim and quant tweak prior to canary start; Marcus will validate telemetry dashboards and SLO config.
5) Communication: I’ll send a short note to the extended CS+Sales list confirming DataSage exclusion and expected timeline.

Attachments: canary-metrics-dash.png (reference mock of the telemetry view).

I’ll follow up with a brief summary to Legal for the exception approval paperwork. If anything changes after the shim lands we’ll reconvene immediately.

—Priya
Priya Natarajan
Program Manager, Model Onboarding & Safety
Redwood Inference
